*Quantization note:* The common default. Good size/quality balance for most local use.

- Memory: lower-precision weights reduce resident size roughly in proportion to the bit width, which is often what decides whether a model fits in VRAM.
- Speed: smaller weights move less data per token, so heavily quantized models are usually faster when memory bandwidth is the bottleneck - but a model that already fits on the GPU may show little difference.
- Quality: quantization is lossy. The loss is usually small at Q5/Q6/Q8 and grows at Q3 and below, and it hits small models harder than large ones.

## 3. Methodology

- Runs per configuration: **5**
- Maximum generated tokens: 1024
- Timeout: 45.0 s
- Streaming: on
- Concurrency: 1 request(s) at a time
- Seed used for determinism tests: 42
- Evaluator: heuristic

**Search strategy**

1. Baseline: the model's own defaults with only an output-token cap, measured first.
2. Warm-up: one unmeasured generation loads the model so the first measured run does not include load time.
3. Coarse search: each generation parameter is varied one at a time (OFAT), so cost grows linearly with the number of parameters instead of multiplicatively.
4. Fine search: the best value of each parameter is combined, and the most influential parameter is probed at neighbouring values.
5. Validation: the top-ranked configurations are re-sampled with additional runs to strengthen their statistics.

**Metrics collected**

- Wall-clock latency measured by the client
- Time to first token (streaming runs only)
- Ollama total_duration, load_duration, prompt_eval_duration, eval_duration
- Prompt tokens and generated tokens as reported by Ollama
- Tokens per second (generated tokens / eval duration)
- System CPU and RAM during each run (psutil, system-wide)
- GPU utilisation and memory (nvidia-smi, when present)

**Evaluation method**

Deterministic heuristics over the produced text.

- correctness: weight 28%
- instruction_following: weight 22%
- completeness: weight 16%
- format_compliance: weight 16%
- relevance: weight 10%
- coherence: weight 8%

- Correctness is only scored where the prompt has a verifiable answer; for open-ended prompts it is reported as not scorable rather than estimated.
- Instruction following counts explicit, checkable constraints (word limits, line counts, forbidden words, required format).
- Consistency combines pairwise content-word similarity across runs with the stability of the quality score.
- Scores measure observable output only. They do not assess hidden reasoning, and for open-ended prompts they do not verify factual accuracy.

- LLM judge: Not used in this experiment.

**Test prompt**

```text
What is you name and how can you help me?
```

## 5. Optimization results

### 5.1 Context optimization

*What changed:* The context window (num_ctx) and/or the layout of the prompt content were changed.

*Why it was tested:* Tests context-window sizes the model actually supports, and - for long prompts - whether trimming or reordering the context changes quality, latency or memory behaviour.

| Configuration | Phase | Quality | Median latency | Tokens/s | Consistency | Failures |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| num_ctx = 8192 | coarse | 8.49 | 4.494 s | 20.2 | 5.19 | 0% |
| num_ctx = 2048 | coarse | 8.54 | 3.375 s | 20.4 | 5.06 | 0% |
| num_ctx = 32768 | coarse | 8.66 | 3.496 s | 20.1 | 5.71 | 0% |

The strongest configuration in this category was 'num_ctx = 32768' (quality 8.66/10, median latency 3.496 s). Quality is 5.5% higher than baseline; median latency is 10.6% slower; the quality difference is within run-to-run noise at this sample size.

- **num_ctx = 8192** - Sets the context window to 8192 tokens (the model declares 32768; this prompt needs roughly 1164). A smaller window reduces KV-cache memory and can speed up prompt evaluation; a larger one costs memory for no benefit when the prompt does not need it. Changing num_ctx reloads the model, so load time is reported separately.
- **num_ctx = 2048** - Sets the context window to 2048 tokens (the model declares 32768; this prompt needs roughly 1164). A smaller window reduces KV-cache memory and can speed up prompt evaluation; a larger one costs memory for no benefit when the prompt does not need it. Changing num_ctx reloads the model, so load time is reported separately.
- **num_ctx = 32768** - Sets the context window to 32768 tokens (the model declares 32768; this prompt needs roughly 1164). A smaller window reduces KV-cache memory and can speed up prompt evaluation; a larger one costs memory for no benefit when the prompt does not need it. Changing num_ctx reloads the model, so load time is reported separately.

The strongest configuration in this category was 'top_p = 0.7' (quality 8.82/10, median latency 4.357 s). Quality is 7.5% higher than baseline; median latency is 37.9% slower; the quality difference is within run-to-run noise at this sample size.

- **repeat_penalty = 1.2** - Penalises tokens that already appeared. Higher values suppress looping but can distort required repetition such as JSON keys or list markers, so both directions are tested.
- **temperature = 1.15 (fine probe)** - Temperature 1.0 won the coarse sweep, so the neighbouring value 1.15 is tested to check whether the coarse grid landed on a local peak or merely near one.
- **top_p = 1.0** - Nucleus sampling keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches top_p. Tightening it trims the low-probability tail, which can reduce drift but also reduce variety.

### 5.3 Prompt optimization

*What changed:* The prompt text was rewritten; the model, sampling settings and system prompt were held constant.

*Why it was tested:* Rewrites the user's prompt into structured variants (explicit task framing, output-format specification, constraints, step decomposition, condensed form) and measures whether the rewrite changes observable output quality.

The strongest configuration in this category was 'Structured task framing' (quality 7.93/10, median latency 1.985 s). Quality is 3.4% lower than baseline; median latency is 37.2% faster; the quality difference is within run-to-run noise at this sample size.

- **Explicit requirements checklist** - Restates the detected constraints as an explicit checklist. Tests whether enumerating requirements improves instruction following.
- **Role and context framing** - Prefixes a short role statement. Tests the common claim that assigning a role improves domain-appropriate output; the claim is measured, not assumed.
- **Output-format specification only** - Adds only the output contract, changing nothing else. Isolates the effect of format instructions from the other rewrites.

*What changed:* Runtime settings were changed: streaming mode, CPU thread count and batch size.

*Why it was tested:* Tests runtime-level settings: streaming versus a single buffered response, CPU thread count, and batch size. Settings that would require reloading the model onto different hardware, or restarting the Ollama server, are reported as not tested.

The strongest configuration in this category was 'Non-streaming response' (quality 8.82/10, median latency 3.419 s). Quality is 7.5% higher than baseline; median latency is 8.2% slower; the quality difference is within run-to-run noise at this sample size.

- **num_batch = 256** - Sets the prompt-processing batch size to 256 (Ollama's default is 512). Larger batches can speed up prompt evaluation at the cost of memory; smaller batches can help on constrained hardware. The effect is mostly on prompt-eval time, so it matters more for long prompts than for long outputs.
- **num_batch = 1024** - Sets the prompt-processing batch size to 1024 (Ollama's default is 512). Larger batches can speed up prompt evaluation at the cost of memory; smaller batches can help on constrained hardware. The effect is mostly on prompt-eval time, so it matters more for long prompts than for long outputs.
- **num_thread = 4** - Pins inference to 4 CPU threads (this machine reports 4 physical / 8 logical cores). More threads are not always faster: oversubscription causes contention, and on a GPU-resident model the setting may have no effect at all. Changing it reloads the model.

- **System prompt: Accuracy-focused** - Tests whether an accuracy directive changes measurable output quality or simply makes the model more hedging.
- **System prompt: task-specific** - A system prompt written for this specific task type. Tests whether task-specific framing beats the generic variants for this workload.
- **System prompt: Minimal system instruction** - The shortest plausible system prompt. Acts as the control for this category: if richer system prompts do not beat it, they are not worth the tokens.

## 8. Recommended configuration

**Model:** qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct

**Objective:** Balanced (Quality (0-10 heuristic score) 40%, Speed (tokens/sec and median latency) 30%, Consistency across repeated runs 30%)

**Configuration:** temperature = 0.0

```json
{
  "num_predict": 1024,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

**Observed results**

- Quality: 8.60/10 95% CI [8.60, 8.60]
- Tokens/sec: 21.2
- Median latency: 3.88 s
- Consistency: 9.95/10
- Successful runs: 7

**Compared with baseline**

- Quality: +4.8%
- Tokens/sec: -16.2%
- Median latency: +22.7%
- Consistency: +143.3%

**Why this configuration was selected**

'temperature = 0.0' ranked first. Quality (0-10 heuristic score) scored 7.80/10 and carries weight 40%, contributing 3.12; Speed (tokens/sec and median latency) scored 3.69/10 and carries weight 30%, contributing 1.11; Consistency across repeated runs scored 9.92/10 and carries weight 30%, contributing 2.98. The weighted contributions sum to 7.20 over 100% of the available weight, giving a composite score of 7.20/10. Against baseline: Quality is 4.8% higher than baseline; median latency is 22.7% slower; the quality difference is within run-to-run noise at this sample size.

> Based on the selected evaluation weights and this benchmark's results, this configuration achieved the highest composite score. It is not a universally optimal setting: a different prompt, a different objective or different hardware can change the ranking.

**How to apply it**

```bash
curl http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d '{
  "model": "qwen2.5:0.5b-instruct",
  "prompt": "YOUR PROMPT HERE",
  "stream": false,
  "options": {
    "num_predict": 1024,
    "temperature": 0.0
  }
}'
```

These are request-time settings only. Nothing in your Ollama installation was changed by this benchmark. To use them, pass the options with your API request or set them in your client; no Modelfile edit is required.

## 10. Not tested

| Item | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| num_gpu (GPU layer offload) | Not tested | Hardware dependent. Choosing a layer count blind would force a model reload and could move the model onto the CPU, invalidating the rest of the benchmark. |
| keep_alive = 0 (unload between runs) | Not tested | Unloading the model after each request would charge the next configuration with the load time, corrupting the comparison. All runs use keep_alive from settings so the model stays resident. |
| OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL / OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS | Not tested | Server-level environment variables. Applying them requires restarting the Ollama service, which this application will not do to your installation. |
| Concurrent request throughput | Not tested | Benchmark requests are issued with the configured concurrency limit (default 1) so that latency measurements reflect the model, not queueing against itself. |
| Quantization comparison | Informational / not directly tested | No alternative local quantized variant of this model family is installed, so quantization is reported as information only. This application does not download, convert or replace model files. |

## 12. Limitations

**Sample size.** Each configuration was measured 5 times (top configurations were re-sampled with extra runs). That is enough to expose large differences, but differences of a few percent are likely to be noise. Confidence intervals are reported with every mean; where they overlap, treat the configurations as indistinguishable.

**Prompt dependence.** Results apply to the prompt that was benchmarked. A configuration that helps a JSON-extraction prompt may hurt creative writing. Re-run the benchmark with a prompt representative of your workload before adopting a setting broadly.

**Stochastic generation.** Unless a seed is fixed, the model samples differently on every run. Some of the variation between configurations is sampling noise rather than a real effect of the setting.

**Evaluator limitations.** Quality scores are deterministic heuristics over the visible output: format checks, explicit-constraint checks, answer-pattern matching and repetition detection. They do not verify factual accuracy for open-ended prompts and they do not measure reasoning. A human reading the raw outputs may reasonably disagree with them.

**Hardware dependence.** Latency and throughput reflect this machine and its load at the time of the run. Results will differ on other hardware, and background activity on this machine can move the numbers.

**Runtime and version differences.** Measured against Ollama 0.34.2. Other versions may change default parameters, scheduling, and which options are honoured.

**Unavailable metrics.** The following were not measurable on this system and are reported as N/A rather than estimated: GPU utilisation and GPU memory (nvidia-smi unavailable); time to first token (non-streaming runs).

**Scope of changes.** Every configuration in this report is a request-time setting. No model file, Modelfile, Ollama setting or system configuration was modified, and nothing needs to be undone.
